title: vinylM5Dial 1.0 Dial virtual-device no-frame attribution

hardware.reason: No matching physical Dial fixture was used; all execution is virtual-device validation.

execution.environment: Device Service native QEMU, ESP32-S3, m5dial profile
execution.reproduction: upload merged BIN as artifact, create firmware for dial, create session, poll serial/frame/wait for 60-120 s
execution.offline_probe: same qemu-system-xtensa -M m5dial on a copy of the session virtual flash, QMP PC/PS/CCOUNT sampling and panel presentation read

checks.name: evidence_intake
checks.detail: analysis, execution-plan, wait, logs, serial, qom-before/after/diff, flash-before/after/diff and observation were read without modification.

checks.name: rom_flash_boot
checks.detail: Serial shows ROM banner, three load segments and entry; the bootloader is at 0x0, which is correct for ESP32-S3.

checks.name: qemu_lifecycle_no_assert
checks.detail: Session state stayed running; no panic, assert, Guru Meditation, reboot banner or QEMU exit was captured.

checks.name: application_segments_loaded
checks.detail: App0 DRAM at 0x3fc94c00 and IRAM at 0x40374000 match the image bytes in the independent probe, so the bootloader completed image load.

checks.name: application_alive
checks.detail: UART1 receives the 5-byte 04 fb 01 08 08 packet every ~2.7 s, matching the firmware's own PORT B 9600 bps string.

checks.name: panel_initialisation_absent
checks.detail: Panel presentation reports generation=1 and madctl=0; the guest never issued a MADCTL write, while the 240x240 frame stays at the 248-byte all-black fallback.

checks.name: same_board_reference_frame
checks.detail: Official UIFlow2 v2.5.3 Dial image on the same machine produced 394 bytes of application serial and a 19,838-byte non-black 240x240 frame with generation=2 and madctl=8.

checks.name: shared_boot_stage_messages
checks.detail: Target and reference both trigger the same M25P80 probe messages and 0x10200C read notice; they are not the discriminator.

checks.name: emulator_model_defect_attribution
checks.detail: No fixed-PC assertion, register readback mismatch or missing device/bus was reproduced; the control firmware proves the Dial display path works.

checks.name: firmware_attribution
checks.detail: No panic or assert marker exists and the application is still running, so the firmware is not blamed either.

checks.name: application_usb_cdc_log
checks.detail: The dial machine's misc.esp32c3.usb_serial_jtag has an empty chardev, so the firmware's own boot diagnostics are not captured.

checks.name: physical_dial_validation
checks.detail: No physical Dial fixture was used.

notes: No emulator code was changed, nothing was pushed to the emulator repository, and no issue was opened because the failure could not be attributed to a reproducible model defect.
Review verdict remains manual_review with E_NO_FRAME; the control firmware result does not transfer to the Arduino lib builder path.
Raw session identities and absolute paths are intentionally omitted.
